R-1.6.owning_step: S2 (C5: 'the data file holds it under version 1')
R-1.6.why_survived: Weak assertion: the case reads the data file but only after assigning dana ('tickets[0].assignee === dana'); the null case (unassigned ticket's record carries assignee: null) is never read. The loader maps a missing key to null (the legacy rule), so every behavioural test passes when the key is omitted.

R-1.13.owning_step: S2 (C6: invalid stored assignee refused at load)
R-1.13.why_survived: Weak case list: the refusal cases are [42, ' ', 65 chars, tab]; the empty string named in R-1.4 ('empty') is not among them, and ' ' is a different value.

R-2.9.owning_step: S3 (C7: 400 for a non-string non-null value)
R-2.9.why_survived: Weak case: the wrong-type member is only 7 (a number); R-4.2 adds 42 and true. No array or object value is tried, so a coercion that only affects them passes.

R-4.7.why_survived: Weak case: the control-character member is a tab only. A newline or carriage return ('a multi-line string' in R-4) is never submitted, and the validator's CONTROL class is not unit-tested per member.
R-4.7.request_clause: S3 (single-line name; the request says 'a non-empty name')

R-4.8.why_survived: Absent for the 'other C0 controls' members: only the tab is submitted.

R-4.9.why_survived: Absent for DEL: only the tab is submitted.

R-5.3.claimed_by: R-5.1 (test/assignment.test.js), 'open and in-progress tickets both accept assignment'
R-5.3.owning_step: S1 (C2) - C2 and R-5.1 name assignment only; the 'and unassignment' half of the R-5 text was dropped when the criterion was written
R-5.3.why_survived: Absent: unassignment is exercised on open tickets (R-3.1, R-3.2) and refused on a resolved one (R-5.3); an in_progress ticket is never unassigned. The test case R-5.1 and criterion C2 narrowed the requirement to assignment.
R-5.3.request_clause: S4 (only open and in-progress tickets can be assigned or unassigned)

R-6.7.owning_step: S1 (C3: 'a no-op appends none', R-6.1) - cross-requirement with R-2.3 trimming
R-6.7.why_survived: Absent: the no-op case R-6.1 submits the exact stored name; the trimming case R-2.3 uses fresh tickets. Nothing submits a padded name for a ticket that already has that agent, so comparing before trimming goes unseen.
R-6.7.request_clause: S5 (assigning the agent a ticket already has changes nothing)

R-7.5.claimed_by: R-6.2 (test/assignment.test.js), 'one audit entry, one notice and a new updated'
R-7.5.why_survived: Weak assertion: R-6.2 checks the entry count and the action of the last entry only; R-7.1 pins {from: null, to: dana} and R-7.2 pins {from: dana, to: null}, but no case pins {from, to} for a reassignment between two agents.

R-7.7.why_survived: Absent: R-7.1 always sends X-Actor, so the 'system' default on the assignment path is never exercised (the actorOf unit test in http.test.js covers the helper, not the route).
R-7.7.request_clause: (audit actor rule - not a request sentence)

R-8.10.claimed_by: R-8.2 (test/assignment.test.js), 'the same pending agent is not queued twice'
R-8.10.why_survived: Weak assertion that cannot discriminate: the same-agent PUT is tried only while the first notice is still pending, where the outbox key dedupes anyway; a store that tries to enqueue on a same-agent assignment is invisible until the first notice has been delivered.

R-8.14.claimed_by: none for ticket.assigned (test/worker.test.js 'gives up after 5 attempts and leaves the event dead' covers the generic rule with another event type)
R-8.14.owning_step: none: no criterion or case names a failing ticket.assigned delivery
R-8.14.why_survived: Absent for this event type: no assignment-specific failure case; the variant is type-specific, so only a failing-delivery case for ticket.assigned would catch it. The operations probe observed a dead event outside the suite.

R-8.15.claimed_by: R-8.2 (test/assignment.test.js), A to B to A
R-8.15.why_survived: Absent state: the A to B to A case runs with A's notice still pending; the case 'return to an agent whose earlier notice was already delivered gets a fresh notice' is never run (SYS-NOTICE delivers dana then bob but never returns to dana).
R-8.15.request_clause: S7 (the agent a ticket is assigned to is notified)

R-9.6.claimed_by: none for the three-way (R-9.2 covers status+priority and assignee+status pairs); C11 names 'combines assignee with priority' but only the scratch proof script w1-s4.js checks it, not the repo suite
R-9.6.why_survived: Absent: the combination cases are pairs. No case combines assignee with priority or all three filters, so dropping priority when an assignee filter is present passes.
